text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Tax talks between government and opposition to take place next Tuesday; ruling coalition wants to force pace
- Trade union federation (DGB) urges government to do more for unemployed; employers' federation chairman Hundt says employers have done their part
- Number of unemployed falls owing to better weather
- Former east German collective farms must pay off debts incurred under communism, court rules
- FAZ economic indicator rises in February
- Housing industry criticises planned tax reform
HANDELSBLATT
- Prospects for jobs market remain poor despite fall in unemployment
- Former east German collective farms must pay off debts incurred under communism, court rules
- Tax talks between government and opposition to take place next Tuesday
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel criticises Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel over comments on monetary union, says he needs no advice
- Job losses in electronics industry to continue, despite business growth
- Hoechst gives up rights to its "abortion pill" RU486
- SAP wants to widen customer base
- Islamists becoming more active in Germany, interior minister says
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Former east German collective farms must pay off debts incurred under communism, court rules
- Tax talks between government and opposition to take place next Tuesday
- Number of crimes with extreme right-wing motives rises
- New chairman of German Farmers' Association takes office
- Chile offers opportunities for German firms to secure contracts worth billions of marks, German transport minister says
- Hoechst gives up rights to its "abortion pill" RU486
DIE WELT
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel criticises Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel over comments on monetary union, says he needs no advice
- Cyanide found in Thomy mustard as blackmailer threatens
- Number of crimes with extreme right-wing motives rises
- Trade union federation (DGB) calls for pact against unemployment
- DGB modifies its positive attitude to monetary union
- Employers continue to cut number of training places
- Construction industry says cut in statutory sick pay has reduced number of absences
